articles.title: Legends' El Clásico Comes to Kolkata: Barcelona and Real Madrid Greats Set for November 25 at Salt Lake Stadium
articles.excerpt: West Bengal sports minister Indranil Khan announced the exhibition on Tuesday. Luís Figo, Iker Casillas and Carles Puyol are reported as potential attractions, though final squads, kick-off time and ticket details are yet to be confirmed.
articles.nri_angle: Legends fixtures are the Indian football calendar's most reliable stadium-fillers; diaspora fans visiting Kolkata in late November get a Salt Lake Stadium night built on the rivalry many of them grew up watching on television.

articles.title: Krishan Pathak Returns as India Name Squad for Home Asian Champions Trophy in Punjab
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Singh captains an 18-member squad for the October 27–November 5 tournament in Jalandhar and Mohali. Defending champions India — five-time winners — keep the core of the Asian Games gold side, with Amandeep Lakra and Aditya Arjun Lalage the young faces retained.
articles.nri_angle: A home tournament in Punjab — the nursery of Indian hockey and the ancestral home of a large share of the diaspora — gives NRI fans a rare major event to plan travel around, with league matches in Jalandhar through November 2.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shubman Gill Wins Record Fifth ICC Award as Shafali Verma Completes Double
articles.excerpt: Gill's 110 and 223 against the West Indies earned him a fifth ICC Player of the Month award for September, while Verma's Asia Cup and Asian Games performances gave India both honours for a third time.
articles.image_caption: Shubman Gill. Gill won a record fifth ICC Player of the Month award, with Shafali Verma completing an Indian double.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora cricket fans, two Indian captains-in-waiting dominating a global monthly award underlines India's depth in both men's and women's cricket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Maaya Rajeshwaran, 17, Wins First Pro Title and Breaks Sania Mirza's 22-Year Record
articles.excerpt: The Coimbatore teenager swept the singles and doubles at the W35 Lagos event in Portugal, beating the top seed from 0-5 down — and becoming the youngest Indian woman to win a W35 singles crown.
articles.image_caption: Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi in action on court. The 17-year-old won her first professional singles title at the W35 Lagos tournament in Portugal.
articles.nri_angle: A 17-year-old Indian breaking a Sania Mirza record is the kind of milestone the diaspora's tennis families track — and a name to watch on the senior circuit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shami Takes Four Wickets, Backs Bhuvneshwar, and Questions His Own Exclusion
articles.excerpt: Bengal's 36-year-old seamer returned 4 for 30 against Delhi at Kalyani, then argued Bhuvneshwar Kumar's New Zealand recall should have come long ago.
articles.image_caption: Mohammed Shami bowls during a domestic match in India. Shami took four wickets for Bengal in their Ranji Trophy opener and said Bhuvneshwar Kumar should have been recalled by India long ago.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian diaspora cricket fans following selection from abroad, Shami's spell and comments reopen the debate over whether veteran seam bowlers are judged on form or age.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Recalled for T20I tour of New Zealand

articles.title: Deshpande Hat-Trick Bowls Chandigarh Out for 78 as Mumbai Take Command at Wankhede
articles.excerpt: Tushar Deshpande took 5 for 17, including a hat-trick in the 11th over, on day two of the Ranji Trophy season opener — becoming the sixth Mumbai bowler to take a Ranji hat-trick, and the first to do it at the Wankhede.
articles.image_caption: Tushar Deshpande, the Mumbai fast bowler who took a hat-trick and 5 for 17 against Chandigarh at the Wankhede.
articles.nri_angle: The Ranji Trophy opener doubles as an audition stage for India's pace bench, which diaspora fans will watch closely with a New Zealand Test series ahead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How Virat Kohli's YouTube Clips Helped Nathan McSweeney Beat India's Spinners
articles.excerpt: The Australia A batter studied Kohli and Steve Smith footage to crack India's spin, scoring 194 runs at 64.66 to win Player of the Series in Australia A's 2-1 ODI win over India A.
articles.image_caption: Nathan McSweeney of Australia A poses with the Player of the Series medal in Puducherry. The 27-year-old studied Virat Kohli's YouTube batting videos to prepare for India's spin, then topped the ODI run charts with 194 runs in three innings.
articles.nri_angle: An Australian batter publicly crediting Virat Kohli's technique as the textbook for surviving Indian spin is a genuine measure of Kohli's influence for diaspora cricket fans — and a small point of pride.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: West Indies' Plan B Against Abhishek Sharma Revealed — and It Failed
articles.excerpt: Shamar Springer admitted the visitors shelved their attacking playbook and tried to starve Abhishek of boundaries. Abhishek knew exactly what was coming — and dismantled it anyway.

sources.label: ESPNcricinfo — How Abhishek messed with West Indies' plans

articles.nri_angle: A rare, candid look at how opponents game-plan against India's most destructive young batter — the tactical chess match diaspora cricket fans love to dissect, straight from the players' own words.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 20 Goals, Zero Conceded: India U17 Women Storm Into Back-to-Back Asian Cups
articles.excerpt: A 4-0 win over Malaysia sealed a perfect Group E campaign for the Young Tigresses, making them the first Indian side at any age level to qualify for consecutive Women's Asian Cups.
articles.image_caption: India's U17 women's footballers celebrate during the AFC U17 Women's Asian Cup qualifiers. The team scored 20 goals across three wins to qualify for back-to-back Asian Cups, a first for any Indian side.
articles.nri_angle: A landmark the global Indian diaspora can rally behind — the Young Tigresses' flawless 20-goals-for-zero-against campaign gives fans worldwide a team to follow into China 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shedge and Nigam's 85-Run Stand Saves India A From Whitewash vs Australia A
articles.excerpt: Suryansh Shedge's 66 and Vipraj Nigam's all-round show lifted India A from 159/6 to a 49-run win at Puducherry — Australia A took the series 2–1.
articles.image_caption: A cricket match in progress with the main building of the Hyderabad Public School in the background, in a photograph from the 1940s. Suryansh Shedge (66) and Vipraj Nigam (40) added 85 runs for the seventh wicket as India A beat Australia A by 49 runs in the third unofficial ODI.
articles.nri_angle: India A games are auditions for the senior team — Shedge and Nigam's rescue act puts two IPL-proven youngsters firmly in the selector conversation ahead of the home season diaspora fans follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.venue: Cricket Association Puducherry Siechem Ground, Puducherry

articles.title: Abhishek's 69 and Arshdeep's Three-Fer Power India to 14-Run Win Over West Indies
articles.excerpt: India defended 223 at Indore's Holkar Stadium to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match T20I series — the first successful defense by the team batting first on this tour.
articles.image_caption: Abhishek Sharma bats for India during the third T20I against the West Indies at Indore. His 30-ball 69 powered India to a 14-run win and a 2-1 series lead.
articles.nri_angle: India take a 2-1 series lead into the fourth T20I — a series-clinching win is now one result away, with Abhishek Sharma and Arshdeep Singh giving diaspora fans the headlines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Bhuvneshwar's Recall at 36, Raina Backs Mohammed Shami for India Comeback
articles.excerpt: The former India batter says Shami is "right behind" Bhuvneshwar Kumar after Bhuvi's age-36 recall — but his comeback case rests on domestic form, not Raina's endorsement.
articles.image_caption: Suresh Raina sits on a blue couch in a cricket-themed studio setting. He backed Mohammed Shami for an India comeback while speaking at the Indian Soft Ball Cricket League jersey launch.
articles.nri_angle: The diaspora's cricket fans follow the New Zealand tour closely — a Shami comeback after years out would be one of the season's biggest stories, and his Ranji opener is the audition to watch.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Voll's Unbeaten 131 Outshines Mostary's Historic 118 as Australia Seal ODI Series
articles.excerpt: Sobhana Mostary's record 118 — the first century by a Bangladesh woman against Australia — was eclipsed within hours as Georgia Voll's unbeaten 131 powered a nine-wicket win that sealed the series 2-0.
articles.image_caption: Australia opener Georgia Voll, whose unbeaten 131 sealed the ODI series against Bangladesh at Allan Border Field.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian cricket fans tracking the women's game's power curve, this series is essential viewing: Bangladesh's 195-run fightback shows the growing depth India will face in the next World Cup cycle, while Voll's power-hitting masterclass is the benchmark India's own batters are chasing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICC ODI World Cup 2027: India opens against Australia, faces Pakistan on October 10
articles.excerpt: The 14th edition runs October 2 to November 21, 2027 across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, with 57 matches in 12 venues and a revamped Super Sevens format.
articles.image_caption: Newlands Cricket Ground in Cape Town, where India opens its 2027 ODI World Cup campaign against Australia on October 7.
articles.nri_angle: South Africa's large Indian-origin community will be out in force at Durban and Johannesburg venues, while US-based fans face 4:00 am ET start times for India's matches — and anyone planning travel can register through the ICC's ticket ballot opened alongside the schedule.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Zealand Recall Allen, Ferguson and Seifert for India ODI Series
articles.excerpt: Finn Allen and Lockie Ferguson return to the 50-over setup for the first time since 2023, joining the final two ODIs as New Zealand test their depth a year out from the World Cup.
articles.image_caption: New Zealand pacer Lockie Ferguson, recalled for the ODI series against India.
articles.nri_angle: The Auckland and Hamilton fixtures draw strong Indian-diaspora crowds; the split-squad format gives fans two distinct New Zealand lineups to watch against India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: First ODI at Eden Park, Auckland

articles.title: Ashwin Slams Hope's Tactics: Hosein Spell Like Feeding Goat to Hungry Lion
articles.excerpt: The former India spinner said persisting with Akeal Hosein for three powerplay overs let a struggling Sanju Samson find rhythm — "Samson simply took advantage of the opportunity."
articles.image_caption: Ravichandran Ashwin. The former India off-spinner questioned Shai Hope's captaincy tactics after West Indies' collapse.
articles.nri_angle: Ashwin's YouTube analysis is one of the most watched post-match platforms among Indian cricket fans, and Samson's redemption under selection pressure is a widely debated topic in the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Hit four consecutive boundaries off Hosein.

articles.title: Will O'Rourke Ruled Out of India Series, Targets Australia Test Comeback
articles.excerpt: New Zealand's 25-year-old quick will miss the ODIs and Tests against India as a “precaution,” with the December tour of Australia now his comeback target.
articles.image_caption: New Zealand fast bowler Will O'Rourke in Test whites. The 25-year-old has been ruled out of the home series against India with hamstring and calf injuries.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora cricket fans, O'Rourke's absence removes one of the tour's most compelling subplots — his duel with India's batters — but a depleted New Zealand attack strengthens India's chances of a statement series win.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Can I Do It Again': Harshal Patel Eyes New Ball in Ranji Reboot With Gujarat
articles.excerpt: After 15 years with Haryana, the 35-year-old seamer wants the new ball for Gujarat — and says red-ball grind is the secret behind his white-ball success.
articles.image_caption: Harshal Patel celebrates a wicket for Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the IPL. The 35-year-old seamer has moved to Gujarat for the 2026 Ranji Trophy season and wants to bowl with the new ball.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's cricket fans, Patel's late-career reinvention is proof the domestic grind still matters in the franchise era — and that a bowler written off as a T20 specialist can still chase the new ball at 35.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Unveils 'Dream Olympics', Hands Rs 8.25 Crore to Asian Games and Chess Stars
articles.excerpt: CM C. Joseph Vijay's 'Dream Olympics' gives Asian and Commonwealth medallists Rs 50 lakh a year for training plus monthly stipends, as the state doubles down on converting near-misses into Olympic podiums.
articles.image_caption: Members of the Indian chess contingent hold the tricolour at a medal ceremony. Tamil Nadu honoured its Chess Olympiad and Asian Games medallists with Rs 8.25 crore in incentives at the Dream Olympics launch in Chennai.
articles.nri_angle: Tamil Nadu produced the chess boom's biggest names — Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa — that the Tamil diaspora follows as hometown heroes; the state's sports funding directly shapes their careers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Smriti Mandhana's India Crush Sri Lanka by 147 Runs to Defend Asian Games Cricket Gold
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's team posted 216/3 and bowled Sri Lanka out for 69 in the Aichi-Nagoya final, securing India's first gold of the Games and back-to-back Asian cricket titles.
articles.image_caption: India batter Smriti Mandhana
articles.nri_angle: India's women's cricket stars are diaspora favorites from Melbourne to New York; the back-to-back Asian titles underline the program the global fanbase rallies behind.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shai Hope's Century Powers Record Chase as West Indies Level T20 Series
articles.excerpt: An unbeaten 102 from Shai Hope dragged West Indies past 250 in Ranchi, sealing the highest successful T20I chase in their history and leveling the five-match series 1-1.
articles.image_caption: West Indies captain Shai Hope in action during the second T20I against India in Ranchi. His unbeaten 102 powered West Indies to a record 250-run chase to level the series 1-1.
articles.nri_angle: India–West Indies cricket is a marquee draw for the Indian diaspora in the US and Caribbean, and a record chase keeps a five-match series alive heading into Indore on Sunday.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Zealand Hit by Double Injury Blow Ahead of India T20I Series
articles.excerpt: Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes are ruled out of the five-match series; Josh Clarkson and Blair Tickner join the Black Caps squad for the opener in Christchurch on October 22.
articles.image_caption: Mark Chapman in action for New Zealand. The batter was ruled out of the five-match T20I series against India with a left hamstring tear.
articles.nri_angle: The India tour of New Zealand — a rematch of the 2026 T20 World Cup final — is appointment viewing for diaspora cricket fans, and NZ's depleted squad reshapes the contest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Para-Shooters Allege Selection Fraud, Protest at Asian Para Games Send-Off
articles.excerpt: Akash and Sandeep Kumar questioned their exclusion from the Aichi-Nagoya squad at the Delhi ceremony attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya; PCI chief Devendra Jhajharia called the process "100 per cent fair."
articles.image_caption: A 10m air rifle victory ceremony at the 2018 Summer Youth Olympics. Indian para-shooters Akash and Sandeep Kumar staged a protest at the contingent's New Delhi send-off Thursday, alleging score manipulation in Asian Para Games squad selection.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs follow India's para athletes closely; a transparent selection system is what keeps that trust — and the careers of Indian-origin athletes — intact.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vithya Targets Sub-54 After Smashing PT Usha's 42-Year-Old Record
articles.excerpt: The 28-year-old hurdler became the first Indian woman under 55 seconds at Aichi-Nagoya. She says domestic competition doesn't push her — and she wants to race the world's best to go faster.
articles.image_caption: Vithya Ramraj
articles.nri_angle: Vithya's demand for world-class racing fields abroad is a story diaspora athletics fans know well — India's best need global exposure to become global champions, and sub-54 would make her India's first world-class women's hurdler.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asian Games Gold Medallist Ritu Negi Excluded From Rs 1 Crore Award List
articles.excerpt: Himachal Pradesh raised its cash award for three of its Asian Games kabaddi gold medallists to Rs 1 crore each plus government jobs — leaving out Ritu Negi, the fourth member of the winning squad.
articles.image_caption: Indian kabaddi player Ritu Negi. The Asian Games gold medallist was excluded from the Rs 1 crore award list.
articles.nri_angle: Himachali and Indian diaspora communities celebrating the kabaddi gold will notice the uneven recognition of a gold-winning squad member — a reminder that transparent reward rules matter more than ad hoc generosity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 71% of India's Asian Games Medals Came From Just Five Sports
articles.excerpt: Athletics, shooting, archery, boxing and wrestling produced 60 of India's 85 medals at Aichi-Nagoya 2026 — a concentration that keeps India fourth in Asia but raises questions about Olympic breadth.
articles.image_caption: India's men's hockey team celebrates on the field at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. India finished fourth with 85 medals, but 71% of them came from just five sports: athletics, shooting, archery, boxing and wrestling.
articles.nri_angle: The diaspora follows the Asian Games as a barometer of India's rise — the cricket, kabaddi and hockey golds travelled through community screenings worldwide — but the narrow medal base shows the sports pipeline is still concentrated in a few disciplines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Young Indian Wrestlers Denied US Visas Ahead of U23 World Championships in Las Vegas
articles.excerpt: Nine of 16 Indian wrestlers who appeared for visa interviews at the US Embassy in New Delhi were refused on Wednesday — told they were below 20 and unemployed; the WFI has asked the embassy to reconsider ahead of Thursday’s appointments.
articles.image_caption: Kushti wrestlers grapple in a sand akhara in Varanasi. Young Indian wrestlers were denied US visas ahead of the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas.
articles.nri_angle: Indian fans in the US may watch a home-soil world championship without India's full squad, in a year when young Indians are facing tightened US visa scrutiny across categories.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pramod Bhagat, Bhavina Patel to Lead India at Asian Para Games
articles.excerpt: The two Tokyo Paralympic medallists will carry the tricolour at the opening ceremony in Nagoya as India sends 121 athletes to the October 18–24 Games.
articles.image_caption: Para-badminton star Pramod Bhagat, Tokyo 2020 Paralympic gold medallist, will carry India's flag alongside table-tennis medallist Bhavina Patel at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games opening ceremony.
articles.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora in Japan gets a rare home-soil chance to support the country's para-athletes in person at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sujeet Kalkal's Comeback From 2-9 Down Wins Asian Games Wrestling Gold
articles.excerpt: The 23-year-old Indian beat Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 in the men's 65kg freestyle final at Aichi-Nagoya on October 2, ending India's eight-year wait for an Asian Games wrestling gold.
articles.image_caption: Sujeet Kalkal celebrates with the Indian tricolor after his Asian Games victory. The 23-year-old fought back from 2-9 down to beat Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 in the men's 65kg freestyle final at Aichi-Nagoya on October 2.
articles.nri_angle: A 23-year-old from Bhiwani's stunning comeback ended an eight-year gold drought — the kind of underdog sporting moment that rallies the global Indian diaspora around the tricolor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Big Sister Who Taught India to Win: Harmanpreet Kaur's Captaincy Legacy
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down after 14 years as India women's captain, leaving behind the country's first senior ICC title and a winning culture that will outlast her.
articles.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur, who stepped down this week as India women captain — the most successful captain in women's T20I history with 77 wins.
articles.nri_angle: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as India women's captain, closing a 14-year leadership era crowned by the 2025 ODI World Cup title and the most T20I wins of any captain in history.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Smriti Mandhana Named India Women's Full-Time Captain as Harmanpreet Steps Down
articles.excerpt: The BCCI named Mandhana all-format captain hours after Harmanpreet Kaur stood down following the Asian Games gold; Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma are the new vice-captains.
articles.image_caption: Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma of the India women's cricket team during a match. Mandhana was named full-time captain on Tuesday, with Verma appointed as her T20I vice-captain.
articles.nri_angle: Mandhana is one of the most followed Indian sportswomen globally; her elevation is a landmark moment for young diaspora fans who have watched women's cricket move to prime time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shreyas Iyer's Maiden T20I Ton Powers India to Eight-Wicket Win Over West Indies
articles.excerpt: The India captain's unbeaten 102 off 43 balls — the first T20I hundred by an Indian skipper in a run chase — sealed an eight-wicket win with 32 balls to spare in Lucknow.
articles.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer raises his bat and helmet after reaching his maiden T20I century. His unbeaten 102 off 43 balls powered India to an eight-wicket win over West Indies in the series opener at Lucknow.
articles.nri_angle: A record-setting night for India's T20 captain, delivered hours after the squad returned from Asian Games gold — the kind of statement win diaspora fans watch for as the team builds toward the next World Cup cycle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
